G.0.title: Start here: what DYON is
G.0.lead: DYON is a private notebook for everything you owe and everything you are owed. Not only money — also items, hours, promises and trusts.
G.0.blocks.0.title: Why it exists
G.0.blocks.0.body: The heaviest part of a debt is often not the amount. It is the not-knowing: who exactly, how much, since when, and whether the other person is quietly hurt. Writing it down removes that fog.
G.0.blocks.1.title: What it will never do
G.0.blocks.1.items.0: It never lends you money and never takes a fee from a loan.
G.0.blocks.1.items.1: It never adds interest, late fees or penalties. Not as an option, not anywhere.
G.0.blocks.1.items.2: It never messages anyone for you. You write and send every message yourself.
G.0.blocks.1.items.3: It never shows your debts to anyone. There is no public list, no score sent anywhere.
G.0.blocks.2.body: Everything lives in this browser, on this device. No account, no server. That also means: if you clear your browser data, it is gone — so export a backup now and then.
G.1.title: Your first entry, step by step
G.1.lead: Press the + button in the header (or the big + on your phone). The form asks six small things. Only three are required.
G.1.blocks.0.items.0.v: Is this money/thing going FROM you or TO you? Pick "I owe" or "Owed to me".
G.1.blocks.0.items.1.v: A loan? A shop tab? A borrowed drill? A promise? Pick the closest chip. You can change it later.
G.1.blocks.0.items.2.v: A name, or a nickname if you prefer privacy ("the neighbour"). Required.
G.1.blocks.0.items.3.v: A number and what it is counted in: SAR, EUR, hours, items, grams of gold. Required unless it is a pure promise.
G.1.blocks.0.items.4.v: "Date incurred" is when it happened (required, cannot be in the future). "Due" is optional — "when able" is a perfectly valid answer.
G.1.blocks.0.items.5.v: Private (only you) or Shared (you will send the other person a summary to confirm).
G.1.blocks.1.title: The fastest way
G.1.blocks.1.body: Type a whole sentence in the top box — "Lent Sara 200 euros, she'll pay me back on 1 March" — and press "Read it". DYON fills the fields in for you. It always shows you what it understood before anything is saved; it never guesses silently.
G.1.blocks.2.title: Rough is fine
G.1.blocks.2.body: Do not stall because you cannot remember the exact figure. Write "maybe 300", tick "It's approximate", and tidy it later. A rough written record beats a perfect forgotten one.
G.2.title: Every screen, and what it is for
G.2.lead: The left sidebar (bottom bar on a phone) holds these. Here is when to open each one.
G.2.blocks.0.items.0.v: Your home. The honest whole picture, plus one suggested next step. Open it daily, for a minute.
G.2.blocks.0.items.1.v: Every commitment in one searchable list. Filter by direction, unit or status; toggle "Closed" to see finished ones.
G.2.blocks.0.items.2.v: The same debts seen as relationships. Shows your balance with each person across every unit.
G.2.blocks.0.items.3.v: Only things that need a decision from you: confirmations, respite requests, disputes, settlement offers.
G.2.blocks.0.items.4.v: Due dates on a month grid, so nothing surprises you. Supports Hijri dates.
G.2.blocks.0.items.5.v: The non-money modules. A promised visit, twelve owed hours, your brother's laptop — these weigh on the mind too.
G.2.blocks.0.items.6.v: A kinder order for paying things off, based on what you can really set aside each month. No interest is ever involved.
G.2.blocks.0.items.7.v: Hides all totals and shows one small step. For the evenings when the numbers are too loud.
G.2.blocks.0.items.8.v: Receipts and screenshots attached to records. Each file gets a fingerprint so you can prove it was not altered.
G.2.blocks.0.items.9.v: Your own private statistics, and a printable sheet for your family in case something happens to you.
G.2.blocks.0.items.10.v: Optional. Verses, du'a, an intention pledge and a private spiritual ledger. Off unless you turn it on.
G.3.title: Reading the Overview cards
G.3.lead: Each card answers one question. The small grey code (W-01, W-02…) is just a reference to the specification — ignore it.
G.3.blocks.0.items.0.v: "Where do I actually stand?" One row per currency. Riyals are never added to euros — mixing units would be a lie, so DYON refuses to do it unless you explicitly switch on the converted view.
G.3.blocks.0.items.1.v: "How complete are my records?" NOT how good a person you are, and not a credit score. It counts missing dates, missing descriptions and approximate amounts. It is private and never leaves your device.
G.3.blocks.0.items.2.v: "Who is waiting on me?" This is the only card that cannot be hidden, because someone else is on the other end of it.
G.3.blocks.0.items.3.v: "What is closest?" One item with its buttons right there, so you can act without hunting for it.
G.3.blocks.0.items.4.v: "What is about to land?" Overdue items are amber. Nothing here is ever red — debt is not an emergency siren.
G.3.blocks.0.items.5.v: "What have I closed?" Deliberately placed as prominently as what is overdue, because closure deserves to be seen.
G.3.blocks.0.items.6.v: A weekly 1–5 tap. If this number gets worse while you use DYON, the app is failing you — that is written into its design, not hidden.
G.3.blocks.0.items.7.v: One gentle tip per day, maximum. Never nagging, always dismissible.
G.3.blocks.1.body: Sections like "Progress & wellbeing" start collapsed. Press "Show" to open them; DYON remembers your choice.
G.4.title: The actions on a record
G.4.lead: Tap any commitment to open it. These buttons appear — here is exactly what each one does.
G.4.blocks.0.items.0.v: Log part or all of what was handed over. DYON refuses an amount larger than what remains, so the maths can never go wrong.
G.4.blocks.0.items.1.v: Writes the message for you in the tone you pick, then YOU send it via WhatsApp, SMS or email. Capped at one per record per week, and three per person per month — a hard limit you cannot override, because it protects the friendship.
G.4.blocks.0.items.2.v: The better path when you are the debtor: remember before the other person has to ask. Stays entirely private.
G.4.blocks.0.items.3.v: You are struggling and need more time. This exists so you never have to invent an excuse or avoid someone. Asking honestly is treated as the respectable act it is.
G.4.blocks.0.items.4.v: You are the creditor, giving more time. Sets a new date by agreement.
G.4.blocks.0.items.5.v: Your own word on when you will pay — kept separate from the official due date, because what you promised matters on its own.
G.4.blocks.0.items.6.v: You forgive the debt. It is wiped and the other person owes nothing. You must tick a box to confirm, and you get 24 hours to undo it — after that it is final.
G.4.blocks.0.items.7.v: Different from release: you stop expecting the money, but you have NOT forgiven it. Two different things, kept honestly separate.
G.4.blocks.0.items.8.v: Change the amount, currency or date by mutual agreement. If you change the currency you must record the rate you agreed — DYON will not let that detail go missing.
G.4.blocks.0.items.9.v: Opens a dispute. It records both views side by side and writes a neutral summary. It never escalates, and the tone switches to Neutral automatically.
G.4.blocks.0.items.10.v: Move the debt to a different debtor. Requires you to confirm all three parties agreed.
G.4.blocks.0.items.11.v: Name someone who saw the agreement. They are read-only and can never change anything.
G.5.title: What each status means
G.5.lead: The coloured chip on every record is its status. It moves through a fixed life cycle.
G.5.blocks.0.items.0.v: You shared it; the other person has not confirmed yet.
G.5.blocks.0.items.1.v: Both of you agree on the terms. This is what prevents arguments later.
G.5.blocks.0.items.3.v: Some has been paid or delivered; a balance remains.
G.5.blocks.0.items.4.v: Extra time was granted. No pressure applies during it.
G.5.blocks.0.items.5.v: A disagreement is recorded. Notice the word: discussion, not dispute-as-war.
G.5.blocks.0.items.6.v: New terms were agreed by both sides.
G.5.blocks.0.items.9.v: The creditor stopped expecting it, without forgiving it.
G.5.blocks.0.items.10.v: Closed and filed away. Still searchable under "Closed".
G.6.title: The Arabic words, explained
G.6.lead: DYON uses a few classical terms because they carry meanings English does not. You never need to know them to use the app — but here they are.
G.6.blocks.0.items.0.v: A debt or liability — something owed that is expected to be fulfilled. The app's name.
G.6.blocks.0.items.1.v: A benevolent loan repaid without any increase. This is the only loan model DYON has — which is why no interest field exists anywhere.
G.6.blocks.0.items.2.v: A trust: something you hold on someone else's behalf and must return — their savings, their laptop.
G.6.blocks.0.items.3.v: A promise you made. Scholars differ on whether it binds legally; many hold it binding morally.
G.6.blocks.0.items.4.v: Granting more time to someone in hardship. In the Qur'an this is an instruction, not a favour (2:280).
G.6.blocks.0.items.5.v: Releasing someone from a debt entirely — forgiving it.
G.6.blocks.0.items.6.v: An amicable settlement when two people see things differently. "And settlement is better" (4:128).
G.6.blocks.0.items.7.v: Transferring a debt to a different debtor, with everyone's consent.
G.6.blocks.0.items.8.v: A guarantee: a third person who joins in the responsibility.
G.6.blocks.0.items.9.v: Delaying payment when you are actually able to pay. DYON never labels anyone with this — only you can say whether you are able or in hardship.
G.6.blocks.0.items.10.v: Hardship. You declare it yourself in Settings; reminders then soften to a respite framing.
G.6.blocks.0.items.11.v: Interest or usury — forbidden. DYON has no field, no formula and no feature for it, anywhere.
G.6.blocks.0.items.12.v: A will. Debts are settled before any inheritance is divided (4:11–12), which is why the Estate sheet exists.
G.6.blocks.0.items.13.v: Truthfulness. In this app it means the history can never be edited silently — every change is kept with its trace.
G.6.blocks.1.body: All religious content here is educational and carries its source. It is not a fatwa — for a ruling, ask a qualified scholar.
G.7.title: Money, units and currencies
G.7.lead: One rule governs everything here: a debt is owed in the unit it was created in.
G.7.blocks.0.title: What that means in practice
G.7.blocks.0.items.0: If you borrowed 2,000 SAR, you owe 2,000 SAR — never a figure recalculated by an exchange rate.
G.7.blocks.0.items.1: Converted totals are display-only and OFF by default. When on, the rate and its date are always shown.
G.7.blocks.0.items.2: Changing a debt's currency only happens through an explicit settlement that records the agreed rate.
G.7.blocks.0.items.3: Amounts are stored as whole numbers of the smallest unit (fils, cents), so rounding errors cannot creep in.
G.7.blocks.1.title: Units you can use
G.7.blocks.1.items.0.v: Standard world currencies, each with its correct number of decimals — JPY has none, KWD has three.
G.7.blocks.1.items.1.v: In grams, with purity (24k, 21k, 18k). Useful where inflation makes a currency figure meaningless.
G.7.blocks.1.items.2.v: For owed work and covered shifts.
G.7.blocks.1.items.3.v: For a borrowed drill, an unfinished job, a wedding gift owed in return.
G.7.blocks.1.items.4.v: No number at all — just done or not done.
G.7.blocks.2.title: High inflation
G.7.blocks.2.body: Whether a debt should be adjusted for severe inflation is a genuinely contested question among scholars and lawyers. DYON refuses to decide it for you: it records what you both agreed and never adjusts anything automatically. You can add a gold reference note at creation as a shared memory of value.
G.8.title: Sharing, reminders and asking without shame
G.8.lead: The hardest part of lending is asking for it back. These tools exist for exactly that moment.
G.8.blocks.0.items.0.v: Writes a polite summary of the record. You send it through your own WhatsApp, SMS or email. DYON has no contact list and messages nobody.
G.8.blocks.0.items.1.v: When they answer, press Confirmed, Requested an edit, or I see this differently. The record now reflects both of you.
G.8.blocks.0.items.2.v: Gentle, Neutral, Formal, or Islamic-gentle. Pick what fits the relationship, not what applies the most pressure.
G.8.blocks.0.items.3.v: Frames the ask as routine bookkeeping — "I'm tidying my records and it shows…" — which removes the sting without deceiving anyone. You still send it yourself.
G.8.blocks.1.title: Protections you cannot switch off
G.8.blocks.1.items.0: One reminder per record per week; three per person per month. Hard limits.
G.8.blocks.1.items.1: Reminders go only to the other party — never to their family, employer or anyone else.
G.8.blocks.1.items.2: Threatening or shaming wording is blocked from being sent, in Arabic and English.
G.8.blocks.1.items.3: If someone declares hardship, reminders automatically soften to talk about timing, not payment.
G.9.title: Privacy, safety and your data
G.9.lead: Honest answers about where your information lives and what protects it.
G.9.blocks.0.items.0.v: In this browser on this device, in a local database. It is never uploaded, because there is no server to upload it to.
G.9.blocks.0.items.1.v: Hides every figure behind a blur; tap one to reveal it. For buses, cafés and shared desks.
G.9.blocks.0.items.2.v: Renames the app to a neutral "Notes". Intended for people who are not safe to be seen tracking debts.
G.9.blocks.0.items.3.v: It stops a casual glance, nothing more. The data sits unencrypted in your browser, so anyone with your unlocked device and a little knowledge can read it. A page like this genuinely cannot provide real security, and pretending otherwise would be dishonest.
G.9.blocks.0.items.4.v: People who do not use DYON are stored as the bare minimum: a name or alias. You can erase a person's details at any time and keep your own record under an alias.
G.9.blocks.0.items.5.v: Settings → Export everything gives you a JSON file. Keep it somewhere safe; it is your only copy.
G.9.blocks.0.items.6.v: Missed fasts and similar. It is off by default, never counted in any total, and excluded from exports unless you opt in item by item.
G.10.title: A gentle routine, and what to do when it feels heavy
G.10.lead: DYON is not trying to keep you here. It is trying to make a hard thing lighter, then let you leave.
G.10.blocks.0.items.0.v: Do the brain dump. Ten categories, rough numbers, no judgment. Most people are surprised by how much they were carrying unwritten.
G.10.blocks.0.items.1.v: Open the Overview. Do the one suggested step. Close the app. That is the whole discipline.
G.10.blocks.0.items.2.v: Answer the 1–5 check-in truthfully. It is private, and it is how you find out whether this is actually helping.
G.10.blocks.0.items.3.v: Turn on Calm mode. Totals vanish, one kind step remains, and there is a 30-second breathing prompt. Nothing is deleted — it is just out of sight until you are ready.
G.10.blocks.1.title: If it is more than heavy
G.10.blocks.1.body: This app is not therapy and not legal advice. If debt is affecting your sleep, health or safety, please speak to a person — the Calm screen lists international helpline directories.
G.10.blocks.2.title: Keyboard shortcuts
G.10.blocks.2.items.2: / — jump to search in the Ledger
G.11.title: Accounts: when DYON asks you to sign in
G.11.lead: DYON starts with no account at all. It only asks you to link a social account when something you do reaches another person.
G.11.blocks.0.title: The two stages
G.11.blocks.0.items.0.v: Adding, editing, paying, releasing, plans, calm mode, the vault, export and delete. Stored in this browser (IndexedDB). No sign-in, ever.
G.11.blocks.0.items.1.v: Sharing a record for confirmation, sending a reminder or a thank-you, inviting a witness, proposing a settlement (ṣulḥ) or a transfer (ḥawālah). These involve someone else, so DYON asks who you are.
G.11.blocks.0.items.2.v: Google, Apple or Microsoft. There are no DYON passwords to create, forget or leak.
G.11.blocks.0.items.3.v: Your name and email from the provider. Nothing is posted, no contacts are read, and your records are not uploaded.
G.11.blocks.0.items.4.v: On a copy where no provider is set up yet, sign-in runs as a clearly labelled preview. It lets you try the flows but is never a verified identity.
G.11.blocks.0.items.5.v: Every request you send — confirm, reminder, respite, settlement, witness, thank-you — has a "QR code" button. It shows a code with the DYON mark in the middle that the other person scans with their camera. It opens that one request only, and they can add it to their own ledger after checking it. Nothing is uploaded.
G.11.blocks.0.items.6.v: Settings → Account → Sign out. Your ledger stays exactly where it is.
G.11.blocks.1.body: If you tap Share while signed out, DYON explains why, lets you sign in, and then brings you straight back to what you were doing.
G.12.title: Every setting, and what it changes
G.12.lead: Settings are grouped in the order you are likely to need them. Nothing here is required to start.
G.12.blocks.0.title: Language & display
G.12.blocks.0.items.0.v: Used only in the greeting. Stays on this device.
G.12.blocks.0.items.1.v: English or Arabic. Arabic mirrors the whole layout right-to-left.
G.12.blocks.0.items.2.v: Western (123), Arabic-Indic (١٢٣) or Persian (۱۲۳). Display only — input accepts all three.
G.12.blocks.0.items.3.v: Show dates in Gregorian, Hijri (Umm al-Qura or civil) or Persian, optionally with a second one beside it. The second list hides whatever the first already uses.
G.12.blocks.0.items.4.v: Shapes the calendar grid; light, dark or follow the system.
G.12.blocks.1.title: Currencies & units
G.12.blocks.1.items.0.v: The default for new entries, and the target of the optional converted view.
G.12.blocks.1.items.1.v: Off by default. When on, adds an indicative total in the base currency. It never changes a debt.
G.12.blocks.2.title: Reminders
G.12.blocks.2.items.0.v: Gentle, neutral, formal (or Islamic when that mode is on) for message templates.
G.12.blocks.2.items.1.v: No reminder suggestions between these times. The end time must differ from the start.
G.12.blocks.2.items.2.v: Nudges to yourself only, never to anyone else.
G.12.blocks.3.title: Privacy & modes
G.12.blocks.3.items.0.v: The spiritual ledger is part of Islamic mode, so its switch only appears once Islamic mode is on.
G.12.blocks.3.items.1.v: A local convenience to keep casual eyes out — not real security.
T..0.title: Everything starts here
T..0.body: Press + to write down anything owed — money, an item, an hour, a promise. On a keyboard you can also press N.
T..1.title: Your honest position
T..1.body: One row per currency or unit. Riyals are never secretly added to euros — mixing units would be a lie. Tap a row to see those records.
T..2.title: Clarity, not judgment
T..2.body: This measures how complete your records are — never how good you are. It is private and never leaves this device.
T..3.title: Who is waiting on you
T..3.body: The one card that can never be hidden, because a real person is on the other end of each item.
T..4.title: Fold what you do not need
T..4.body: Each band of cards can be hidden or shown. DYON remembers your choice on this device.
T..5.title: When it feels too loud
T..5.body: Calm mode hides every total and leaves one kind step. Nothing is deleted; it just waits for you.
T..6.title: Arabic & English
T..6.body: Switch language any time. The whole layout mirrors for Arabic, and you can use Arabic-Indic digits and Hijri dates.
T..7.title: No account needed — until you share
T..7.body: Your ledger lives in this browser. You only link a Google, Apple or Microsoft account when you share, remind or invite someone.
T..8.title: Every other screen
T..8.body: On a phone, More holds every screen plus quick switches for theme, calm mode, the tour and your account.
T..9.title: Help is always one tap away
T..9.body: The ? button explains the screen you are on, starts its tour, and opens the full guide and A–Z glossary.
T.onboarding.0.title: Language and Islamic mode
T.onboarding.0.body: Pick your language first. Islamic mode is optional and off by default; you can change both later in Settings.
T.onboarding.1.title: Help while you set up
T.onboarding.1.body: The guide and glossary explain every word. Open them any time and come back here.
T.onboarding.2.title: Empty your head, roughly
T.onboarding.2.body: Start writes down what you remember, one category at a time. Rough is fine — you can fix details later. Or skip and add things one by one.
T.ledger.0.title: Find anything
T.ledger.0.body: Search by person, description or type. Press / anywhere to jump here.
T.ledger.1.title: Which way it goes
T.ledger.1.body: Filter to what you owe, what you are owed, or mutual arrangements.
T.ledger.2.title: Unit, order and closed records
T.ledger.2.body: Narrow to one unit, change the order, or show records that are already fulfilled or released.
T.ledger.3.title: Open a record
T.ledger.3.body: Tap any row to see its terms, progress, witnesses, evidence, history — and every action you can take on it.
T.people.0.title: Add a person
T.people.0.body: People are created automatically when you add a record, but you can add one here with a relationship label.
T.people.1.title: Balances per person
T.people.1.body: Each person shows what is open between you, per unit. Tap to see everything with them and settle together.
T.settings.0.title: Your account (optional)
T.settings.0.body: Stage 1 is on-device only. Linking a social account (stage 2) unlocks sharing and reminders. You can sign out any time.
T.settings.1.title: Back up your ledger
T.settings.1.body: Everything lives in this browser. Export a backup now and then — export never needs an account.
